proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 139166 reaches 1 in fewer than 268 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 268.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1523, the stopping time of n is less than 268.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^2 is at least n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^3 is congruent to (n^3) + 85 modulo 5.
The steps above establish the statement up to 1523, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 139166.
